![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14224904/assets/008a79d8328b5b58cdc68a39a921125a1efa7e0b46a663b1ede9dc6773fb48e8.png)

The quarter-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=3$ and $b=1.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14224904/assets/82436a7f248ed63683a3164d8c372433abb6f919567defa05700ebf88c50308f.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
